name: Book Reading and Activity for Children - Stories and games
description: Join us for an engaging session with children's author Mallika Ravikumar, whose football-themed novels The District Cup and The State League have captivated young readers. Come spend an evening filled with stories, sports, and interactive activities. The session will include storytelling, games, conversations about the books, and lots of opportunities to celebrate teamwork and imagination.

name: Not safe for work - Book launch
description:
Join us for the Bangalore launch of Not Safe for Work, the latest contemporary romance by Radhika Agrawal.
Set against the backdrop of corporate chaos, Not Safe for Work follows senior graphic designer Kavya Mehra and her infuriatingly charming intern Neil Desai as workplace rivalry, hidden secrets, and late-night brainstorming sessions blur the lines between professional and personal. Packed with witty banter, sizzling chemistry, and an irresistible enemies-to-lovers romance, it's a must-read for fans of modern rom-coms. 
The evening will feature Radhika in conversation with Aastha Sharma as they discuss writing romance, creating unforgettable characters, navigating the publishing journey, and everything that makes readers fall in love with a great love story.
About the Hosts:
Aastha Sharma is a community builder and tastemaker, founder of HappyStoryNook and The Bookstagram Collective. With 10 years across founders’ offices and marketing for India’s most loved consumer tech and lifestyle brands, she writes on Substack at the intersection of aesthetics, culture, and everyday life.
Radhika Agrawal is a lifestyle journalist and the author of the bestselling romance novel Red Flags and Rishtas. A sucker for all things filmy, she sees the world in meet-cutes and dream sequences. Originally from Delhi, she now lives in Thailand with her husband and their over-pampered dog, who hates competing with fictional characters for her attention.

name: Stories from Puranas - Oral storytelling event
description: Stories from Puranas pulls back the curtains on ancient Indian lore to deliver a thought provoking performance tailored for an adult audience. Unpacking tales from a few of the Mahapuranas, this oral storytelling event by Aparna Jaishankar explores the cosmic gaslighting, bureaucratic loopholes and chaotic choices of gods and mortals alike, that govern the universe.  It connects ancient mythology with modern anxieties, showing that beneath the scared veneer, our oldest legends have always been about us.

name: Coffee and Conversations - Group Meetup by The Listeners Circle
description:
What about some Filter Coffee and Unfiltered conversations on a fine Sunday morning?
Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment.
We at Listeners Circle are committed to building a community where there are no unsaid words, held-back emotions and buried feelings because of the fear of being judged.
After 50+ Editions of Tell Your Story, Listeners Circle is relaunching a lighter format - Coffee and Conversations!
Coffee lightens us up. Coffee gives us clarity. Coffee refreshes. Sip a coffee and speak your heart out without fear of judgment, and listen without judging! Coffee is on us, and the onus of conversation without judgment is on you.
 
Every word matters. Every emotion matters. Every feeling matters.
Think about how it would feel to take an hour out of your fast-paced life and share your experiences and thoughts to people who listen to you without judging over a cup of Coffee? Also, listen to others without judging.
Listeners' Circle Coffee and Conversations -This is an event to make that happen.
Be a part of the Listener's Circle Coffee & Conversations - Edition 5.
Speak your mind without being judged. Speak your mind without any boundaries. No photography and videography without consent. Your stories stay within the four walls of the room and the hearts.
Would you like to just listen? We have a place for you too.
Book your passes in advance to avoid the last-minute sell outs.
Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment. We have done 50+ sessions over the last year, enabling people to voice their stories. Coffee & Conversations is our new format based on popular demand.

name: Girls Who Stray  - Book Talk and Discussion
description:
This event is a discussion with Anisha Lalvani on her debut novel Girls Who Stray, published by Bloomsbury India in 2024. Anisha will be in conversation with cultural practitioner, poet and writer Arundhati Ghosh, whose book of non-fiction All Our Loves: Journeys with Polyamory in India was published by Aleph Book Company in 2025.
About the book:
Girls Who Stray by Anisha Lalvani is a dark coming-of-age thriller set primarily in the Delhi-NCR region. It follows an unnamed, anxious 23-year-old woman navigating an illicit affair with a married property developer that eventually spirals into her getting entangled in a double murder, based on a true crime. The novel explores themes of modernity, alienation, loneliness, modern Indian society, and the heavy consequences of reckless choices. The novel was shortlisted for the Kalinga Literary Festival Book Awards in the English Debut in 2024 and the Crossword Book Awards 2025 in the Jury Awards for Fiction.
About the author:
Anisha Lalvani has a Master’s of Arts degree in English Literature (Honours) from Mumbai University. She has worked in publishing and on various literary projects including the literary television programme Kitaabnama: Books and Beyond, and the Jaipur Literature Festival. She currently works in communications at a leading think tank that engages with the nexus of environment, economic opportunity and human well-being.
About Arundhati Ghosh:
Arundhati is a writer, cultural practitioner, social activist and traveller with three decades of experience including as the Executive Director of India Foundation for the Arts (IFA) (2013- 2023). Her awards include Chevening Clore Leadership, Gurukul Scholarship at London School of Economics and Salzburg Global Fellowship. She contributed on advisory panels of the Seagull Foundation, Blind with Camera, Sangama and Toto funds the Arts, and continues for Museum of Art and Photography, Shomokaleen Protibidhan, Solidarity Foundation, and Maraa. Her poetry in Bangla Oshomoye phire esho nodi hoye was published in January 2023 by Lastrada Prakashan. Her book All Our Loves: Journeys with Polyamory in India was published in 2025 by Aleph Book Company and won the Non Fiction Book of the Year Award at the Rainbow Literature Festival 2025 and the Kala Shreshtha Award for Debut Author English at the Kala Literature Awards 2026. She has also co-edited a collection of essays in Bangla of daughters writing about their mothers titled Meyeder Mayera (Mothers of Daughters) published by Sonta Prokashona in 2026. She writes a monthly column on relationships titled Ties and Knots for the Deccan Herald. She consults and trains for the cultural and not-for-profit sector

name: Live Drawing Bootcamp  - Art Workshop
description:
Live Drawing Bootcamp: Learn how to draw on location and maintain a sketchbook with this 4-part live drawing bootcamp! Each session will begin with an instructional segment, learning an aspect of life drawing and building skills, followed by a live location demo and a practice session for participants. Instructional sessions will be conducted at Atta Galatta, Indiranagar, followed by the demo and drawing session at a different location in the area each week. 
Each week we tackle something different - 
Session 1: Drawing Nature and Organic shapes. 
Session 2: Understanding Perspective and architecture. 
Session 3: Drawing people. 
Session 4: Capturing Light and Colour. 
Dates: Sundays 9 AM-12 PM (3hrs) on 16th Aug, 23rd Aug, 30th Aug & 6th September.
Facilitated by Jyotsna Ramesh (Animator & Illustrator), Instagram: @jojorambles
PLEASE NOTE: the workshop will have 4 sessions conducted on 4 different days, and the price is inclusive of all 4 sessions.

name: Tiny Budget Big Story - Workshop
description:

He will be breaking down his working framework for what to kill, keep, and steal so you can make sharper creative decisions using real-world case studies like Zomato, Fevicol, and Dollar Shave Club. 
Actionable strategies that save you money and leave you with one concrete decision for your business that same week. 
Limited seats.

name: Atta Galatta presents “Support Group” - Support Group
description:
People make up big cities, but what makes up people’s lives, hopefully not loneliness. Loneliness is an intensely painful state that arises out of a lack of intimacy and connectedness. People from every walk of life, even those with social contacts or pursuing successful careers, can experience sadness from the absence of belonging. This painful experience is felt in a myriad of contexts, such as breakups, disagreeing families, fear of rejection, unrelatability, shyness, and so on
This support group has been constituted to bring people struggling with disconnectedness in various contexts together for a shared experience of comfort, belonging, laughter, guidance, and above all, to break the cycle of sustained loneliness
The support is being organized and moderated by Nimesh George and Gokul R, who are practicing psychologists based in Bangalore

name: Curious Minds Trivia Night  - Trivia Night
description:
Forget everything you think a trivia night is. 
Curious Minds Trivia Night is an interactive, people-first experience that blends pop culture, teamwork, strategy, and friendly competition into one memorable evening. Before the event, participants fill out a short registration form sharing their favourite movies, TV shows, music, and interests. Parts of the trivia are then built around those responses, making every edition unique and tailored to the people in the room. Expect a mix of visual rounds, quote challenges, picture rounds, strategic betting rounds, and a few surprises along the way. Some rounds will test your memory, others your observation, and a few will reward teamwork, creativity, and quick thinking.
Whether you’re a seasoned trivia enthusiast or someone looking for a genuinely good evening with strangers — this event is designed to bring people together through laughter, conversation, and a little healthy rivalry.
Come with a team or walk in solo — we’ll find you one. All you need is curiosity and a willingness to play.
Come once. Come back forever

name: TechnoCats - Film Screening
description:
A search for purpose in the fiercely competitive world of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT).
SYNOPSIS 
Seven young people from seven parts of the country (the Seven Samurai) dream of joining the IIT. Competing against one million applicants, they gain admission, but are soon disillusioned. Will they make their presence felt on the world stage? Or burn out along the way? The filmmaker, an IIT alumnus, follows the Seven Samurai over seven years—from their first semester to the third year of their careers. Interwoven with their journey are four of the filmmaker’s classmates from 35 years ago, including one who made an audiovisual on IIT student life. As he rediscovers old slides and struggles to sync them with the audio track, this forgotten past frames the film’s exploration of winning at all cost. 
DIRECTOR’S STATEMENT 
I enrolled for a B.Tech. in electrical engineering at IIT Delhi, but was dejected at the barrage of tests and emphasis on grades over all else. Where was the time to learn, ponder, speculate? 35 years later, I was surprised to meet students from very different backgrounds who felt similarly. I decided to revisit my past and connect with some of my classmates. Their stories are interwoven with  those of the seven students at the heart of this film, to create a conversation across generations.

name: The Next Curve Within - A Quarterly Flagship Experience by The Next Curve
description:
Some of life’s most meaningful transformations don’t begin around us—they begin within us.
The Next Curve Within is the flagship quarterly gathering by The Next Curve, bringing together inspiring voices from leadership, health, longevity, mindfulness and sustainability to help us prepare for the most important years of our lives.
This is not another seminar. It is an immersive afternoon of ideas, lived experiences and authentic conversations designed for those who believe that growing older should mean growing stronger, healthier, wiser and more purposeful.
This edition explores five dimensions of transformation:

Finding clarity through meditation and mindful living.
Building a regenerative future through water and conscious action.
Reinventing life after 75 with purpose and vitality.
Preventing disease by embracing a healthier way of life.
Understanding how healthy, resilient leaders build high-performing organisations through physical, mental and emotional transformation.

Whether you are an entrepreneur, corporate leader, professional, educator, healthcare practitioner, student or someone committed to lifelong growth, Within offers insights that go beyond knowledge and inspire meaningful action.
Event Details
Date: Saturday, 19th September 2026
Time: 3:00 PM – 5:00 PM
Venue: Atta Galatta, Bengaluru
Access Pass: ₹300 per person
Featured Speakers

Cherian Kuruvila – The Quiet Revolution
Vivek Srinivasan – Every Drop Matters
Hari Bhaskaran – Life Begins at 75
Dr. Dharini – Prevention Before Prescription
Keynote: Salma Moosa – Drive to Thrive: Building Fit & Healthy Leaders to Build Fast-Growing Organisations

The evening concludes with Conversations That Matter—a guided networking experience where meaningful connections are built through thoughtful dialogue rather than business card exchanges.
The Next Curve Within is for those ready to reinvent ageing, regenerate the planet and redesign themselves—one conversation at a time.
